validity.recommendation: Keep the row. It is a real, correctly classified gas transmission trunk. Apply the two caveats below (start endpoint + length).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed. IGAT 8 (Iran Gas Trunkline 8 / eighth national gas trunkline, 'خط هشتم سراسری گاز') is well documented by multiple INDEPENDENT sources that name it specifically. Oil & Gas Journal (NIGC infrastructure article) describes 'IGAT VIII' as a 1,050-km, 56-in. line carrying South Pars gas to the Parsian gas plant and north toward a Tehran-serving connection, powered by 10 compressor stations totaling 1.8 million hp. Persian Wikipedia (independent of GEM) gives the same: 56-inch, begins east of Asaluyeh, passes Parsian in Fars, on to Isfahan and Qom provinces. Independent reporting names the five IGAT-8 compressor stations launched March 2017 (Naein, Khonj/Khanj, Safashahr, Jahrom). GulfPub PE World Map also carries an independent 'IGAT 8' record (Assaluyeh -> Qom, 56 in). Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correct — a high-pressure 56-inch national gas TRANSMISSION trunk, not gathering/feeder/plant-internal, and gas (not oil/NGL/condensate). DUPLICATE: none — it is the only IGAT 8 in the 31-row roster; the auto-flagged 'GEM IGAT 9 vs GulfPub IGAT 8' mismatch is fuzzy name cross-pairing, not a real duplicate of P0447. CAVEATS: (1) ATTRIBUTION/endpoint — GEM StartLocation='Parsian Refinery' understates the origin. Every independent source places the origin EAST OF ASALUYEH / South Pars Gas Complex (Jam, Bushehr), with the Parsian refinery a WAYPOINT the line passes, not its head. GulfPub agrees (Assaluyeh -> Qom). Recommend Start = Asaluyeh / South Pars (Bushehr), Parsian demoted to a waypoint; End = Qom is correct. (2) SPEC/length — GEM LengthKnown=1000 km reads slightly low; OGJ and fa.wiki both state 1,050 km. The 1000 is a defensible round-down, not wrong, but 1,050 km is the better-sourced figure. GulfPub's 642 km is the outlier and appears to be a partial/erroneous segment length — do NOT adopt it. SPECS THAT CHECK OUT: Diameter 56 in (OGJ + fa.wiki, high). Capacity 3884.60 MMcf/d is arithmetically the conversion of the widely reported 110 mcm/d (110 x 35.3147 = 3,884.6) — internally consistent and correct; its identity with IGAT 6's 3884.6 is because both lines are rated ~110 mcm/d, NOT a copy-paste placeholder. Owner: GEM lists Iran Ministry of Petroleum 100% — acceptable at parent level, but the OPERATOR is National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), a Ministry subsidiary; consider recording NIGC as operator.

validity.recommendation: Update LengthKnown 1000 -> 1050 km (better-sourced); reject GulfPub's 642 km.
validity.researcher_notes: Length: GEM=1000 km. Oil & Gas Journal states '1,050-km' and Persian Wikipedia states 1,050 km — two independent sources agree on 1,050. GulfPub's 642 km disagrees materially and is not corroborated by any independent source (likely a partial/segment figure); it should NOT be adopted. 1,050 km is the recommended value; the existing 1000 is a low round-down, not a fabrication.

fills.researcher_notes: 56-inch confirmed by OGJ ('56-in. line') and fa.wiki ('۵۶ اینچ') — two independent sources agree with GEM's 56.
OGJ describes IGAT VIII as one of the national gas trunklines carrying South Pars gas to central/northern demand centers — a long-haul high-pressure transmission trunk. Correct classification.
Natural gas trunkline (Iran Gas Trunkline 8) carrying South Pars gas — Fuel=Gas confirmed by OGJ and all sources.

Operating status is well supported: the five IGAT-8 compressor stations (Naein, Khonj, Safashahr, Jahrom) were inaugurated March 2017 and the line is described across independent reporting as an operational NIGC transmission pipeline carrying ~110 mcm/d from South Pars. OGJ documents the built-out compressor fleet. The strongest single dated 'operational' confirmation (Financial Tribune, March 2017) could not be attached because financialtribune.com serves a JS redirect that the url_verifier cannot read — hence tier=medium rather than high. No independent source contradicts 'operating'.

routes.start_name: East of Asaluyeh / South Pars Gas Complex (Jam), Bushehr Province
routes.corridor_desc: Runs from the South Pars coast (east of Asaluyeh, Jam, Bushehr) northeast/north through Fars Province — passing the Parsian refinery near Mohr and the compressor stations at Jahrom and Safashahr — then across Isfahan Province (Nain area) and northwest to the city of Qom in Qom Province. ~1,050 km total. The endpoint cities and the four named compressor-station towns are firmly sourced (OGJ + fa.wiki + independent compressor-launch reporting); the coordinates given are the well-known locations of those NAMED places, not surveyed pipeline vertices, so the corridor is a defensible medium-accuracy chain, not a meter-level trace. GulfPub's 642 km would not span this corridor, reinforcing that its length is partial/wrong.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints and corridor established from OGJ (route to Parsian gas plant and north toward Tehran-serving connection) and fa.wiki (origin east of Asaluyeh -> Parsian, Fars -> Isfahan -> Qom), cross-checked against GulfPub (Assaluyeh -> Qom). Waypoint coordinates are the standard published locations of the named towns/refinery/compressor stations (Asaluyeh 27.48N,52.62E; Parsian/Mohr ~27.55N,52.88E; Jahrom 28.50N,53.56E; Safashahr 30.61N,53.19E; Nain 32.86N,53.08E; Qom 34.64N,50.88E). No coordinate was invented — each is a real, named place from the sourced route. Current GEM endpoints ('Asia'/'Asia', RouteNotes nan) carry no geographic content and should be replaced by this sourced corridor. Note the GEM StartLocation 'Parsian Refinery' is a waypoint, not the true head (Asaluyeh/South Pars).

summary: P0447 IGAT 8 is real, correctly classified (56-in national gas transmission trunk), and unique (no duplicate); confirmed (caveat) — fix start endpoint (Asaluyeh/South Pars, not Parsian Refinery) and length (1050 km, not 1000; reject GulfPub 642); capacity 3884.6 MMcf/d = 110 mcm/d is correct.
